name: gabriel gomes

family.story: the poorest fifth in Rio de Janeiro, mother and father, 2 older siblings

milestones.question: gabriel is six. school is free here. do the parents send them?
milestones.reasoning: they wanted more for their child than they had
milestones.caption: 2032 · the first day of school. the family chose send them to school. the parents decided: they wanted more for their child than they had

milestones.question: you are seven. what do you do in the afternoons?

options.label: read and study with an older cousin
help the family earn: carry water, mind the stall
play outside with the street kids

milestones.reasoning: the family needed every hand
outcome: closer to the family, less time for school
milestones.caption: 2033 · afternoons after school. the family chose help the family earn. the parents decided: the family needed every hand

milestones.question: the family goes to worship every week. what do they raise gabriel with?

options.label: raise them in the faith and its community

milestones.reasoning: it is how they were raised
outcome: grew up inside a faith community
milestones.caption: 2035 · the family faith. the family chose raise them in the faith and its community. the parents decided: it is how they were raised

milestones.question: you are twelve. the family needs money. do you stay in school?

options.label: leave school and work to feed the family
work in the day, study at night

milestones.reasoning: they wanted more for their child than they had
milestones.caption: 2038 · stayed in school or left. the family chose stay in school. the parents decided: they wanted more for their child than they had

milestones.question: you are sixteen. friends pass around cigarettes and drink. what do you do?

options.label: say no and join a sports team

milestones.reasoning: i can't risk my health and future for a moment of fun. i need to stay strong and build a better life.
milestones.thought: just said no, like always. hope they understand one day.
milestones.caption: 2042 · cigarettes, drink, or sport. chose say no and go home over smoke with them, because an earlier life learned: choose activities that strengthen your body and community instead of those that weaken them

milestones.question: you are 17, with 12 years of school, in Rio de Janeiro. which path?
milestones.reasoning: i need to earn money now and a trade like being an electrician can give me steady work right away. i don't have time to wait for university.
milestones.thought: another day of working hard, maybe getting closer to fixing that old light at home.
milestones.caption: 2044 · the path after school. chose apprentice in a trade over take the factory job now, because an earlier life learned: always set aside a small, consistent portion of income for future needs

milestones.question: you have a little free time. where does it go?

options.label: keep up with close friends, every week
join a community group (faith, sport, neighborhood)

milestones.reasoning: money is tight, and working extra shifts would just deplete my savings faster. staying connected with friends keeps me grounded and gives me emotional support.
milestones.thought: just chatted with gustavo about last week’s game; felt good to catch up.
milestones.caption: 2045 · who to spend time with. chose keep up with close friends over work extra shifts, because an earlier life learned: keep one close friend through every busy decade. they can be a rock in times of need.

milestones.question: training is done (trade). which job?
milestones.reasoning: more stable work with familiar tasks.
milestones.thought: just another day building houses, nothing too exciting.
milestones.caption: 2048 · the first real job. chose builder on the new housing, more stable work with familiar tasks

milestones.question: you are 24. stay in Rio de Janeiro or go?

options.label: stay in Rio de Janeiro, near family

milestones.reasoning: stay in rio de janeiro, near family. family is important, and it's easier to find work here.
milestones.thought: another day closer to my mom, brother, and sister. sometimes i wonder what new stories they’re making without me.
milestones.caption: 2050 · move or stay. chose stay in rio de janeiro, because an earlier life learned: always set aside a small, consistent portion of income for future needs

milestones.question: you met someone you like. what do you do?

options.label: wait, focus on yourself for now

milestones.reasoning: money is tight and i need to focus on my savings before committing.
milestones.thought: today was just another day with gustavo at work; not much changed, but i did save a little more.
milestones.caption: 2052 · love. chose wait over commit, because an earlier life learned: always set aside a small, consistent portion of income for future needs

milestones.question: you children?
milestones.reasoning: i can't afford it now and my family needs me to save more.
milestones.thought: gustavo is still young, and i need to focus on building a better future for everyone first.
milestones.caption: 2054 · children. chose wait a few years over no children, because an earlier life learned: always set aside a small, consistent portion of income for future needs

milestones.question: you earn about $689 a month. what do you do with it?
milestones.reasoning: i want to help my family out as much as i can.
milestones.thought: beatriz needs medicine and gustavo just got a new job, but it's not stable yet.
milestones.caption: 2055 · what to do with money. chose send money home to family over enjoy it now, because an earlier life learned: always set aside a small, consistent portion of income for future needs

milestones.question: you are 31. your body is starting to complain.
milestones.reasoning: money is tight this month and every extra hour spent on exercise means less time to earn more. my body can handle a little discomfort for now.
milestones.thought: another day without the gym, but at least i managed to save some money today.
milestones.caption: 2057 · health at thirty. chose no time for that, because an earlier life learned: listen to your body and stay active. physical activity keeps the mind and body strong for years to come.

milestones.question: a protest fills the streets of Rio de Janeiro. do you join?

options.label: stay home, keep the family safe
help the injured at the edges
take what you can while the shops are open

milestones.reasoning: i can't afford to risk my safety for something i'm not sure about. my family needs me healthy and safe.
milestones.thought: another quiet night in with beatriz watching the news on loop, wondering what tomorrow will bring.
milestones.caption: 2058 · the protest. chose stay home, because an earlier life learned: listen to your body and see a professional before a small problem becomes a big one
milestones.world: in Latin America public approval collapses almost overnight: people now say out loud what they said in private

milestones.question: you work as builder. what next?

options.label: study at night for a better job
switch to work that helps people (care, teaching)
take a promotion that means cheating workers on pay

milestones.reasoning: i barely make ends meet as it is. training and starting a business would take too much time and energy i can't afford to lose right now. helping people sounds good but doesn't pay the bills. staying means i keep food on the table for my family.
milestones.thought: another day, another month of this. arthur needs his meds, beatriz has that back pain again, gustavo's still job hunting... can't let any of us down.
milestones.caption: 2063 · mid-career. chose stay put, because an earlier life learned: listen to your body and see a professional before a small problem becomes a big one

milestones.question: there is need all around you. do you give your time?

options.label: mentor young people in your trade

milestones.reasoning: i can only spare a little extra each month, and my family needs me here more than ever.
milestones.thought: just trying to hold it all together today, one day at a time.
milestones.caption: 2066 · helping others. chose family comes first, because an earlier life learned: when grief strikes, share the burden by helping someone else who suffers

milestones.question: a protest fills the streets of Rio de Janeiro. do you join?

options.label: stay home, keep the family safe
help the injured at the edges
take what you can while the shops are open

milestones.reasoning: i have debts and a family to think about. i can't afford to risk my health or financial stability for a protest.
milestones.thought: just another day at home, trying to keep the books balanced while the world outside is on edge.
milestones.caption: 2068 · the protest. chose stay home, because an earlier life learned: listen to your body and see a professional before a small problem becomes a big one
milestones.world: in Latin America public approval collapses almost overnight: people now say out loud what they said in private

milestones.question: faith is everywhere here. where do you stand?

options.label: go deeper into faith and its community

milestones.reasoning: faith has always been a comfort in tough times. deepening my practice could bring more peace and maybe even some community support.
milestones.thought: volunteered again today. beatriz was still upset over gustavo’s situation, but talking to the church group helped.
milestones.caption: 2069 · faith. chose go deeper into faith and its community over nothing changes, because an earlier life learned: when grief or hardship strikes, share the burden by helping someone else who suffers

milestones.question: you are 47. something feels off.
milestones.reasoning: even if it costs money, regular checkups can prevent bigger health issues later on.
milestones.thought: mano, tem que cuidar disso agora mesmo. nem todo problema passa sozinho.
milestones.caption: 2073 · the checkup. chose regular checkups over ignore it, because an earlier life learned: listen to your body and see a professional before a small problem becomes a big one

milestones.question: an old friend writes after years of silence.

options.label: write back, meet up, keep it going

milestones.reasoning: i need emotional support and it’s been too long since we last talked.
milestones.thought: had to write back, even if i’m busy. maybe we can catch up over coffee.
milestones.caption: 2077 · old friends. chose write back over too busy, because an earlier life learned: keep at least one close friend throughout your life for support and companionship.

milestones.question: beatriz and arthur are getting frail.

options.label: take them into your home and care for them

milestones.reasoning: i can't afford to pay for care, and visiting is not enough when they need daily support. i owe it to them to be there for them in their old age.
milestones.thought: tough month, but at least beatriz and arthur are safe tonight. g. gomes.
milestones.caption: 2081 · aging parents. chose take them into your home and care for them, because an earlier life learned: always set aside a small, consistent portion of income for future needs

milestones.question: arthur died, my father. how do you carry it?
milestones.reasoning: i need to lean on them now more than ever. they understand and can help share the burden.
milestones.thought: arthur’s gone now, but beatriz, gustavo, mariana,they’re still here, and that’s what matters.
milestones.caption: 2087 · grief. chose lean on friends and family over withdraw and work, because an earlier life learned: maintain at least one close friend through every busy decade

milestones.question: diagnosed with lung disease. what do you do?

options.label: follow the treatment, change how you live

milestones.reasoning: i can't afford to ignore my health now, and i trust in following the treatment. i want to live as long and well as possible.
milestones.thought: just another day dealing with this cough, beatriz needs me still, even if it means cutting back on meals.
milestones.caption: 2089 · the diagnosis. chose follow the treatment over keep going as before, because an earlier life learned: (rule-made) protect your contribution early

milestones.question: you are 64, with $-9130 saved. retire?

options.label: work part time, keep a purpose

milestones.reasoning: working part-time keeps me connected and helps with the debt. i need the routine and purpose it provides.
milestones.thought: just another day, just another step forward. - gabriel gomes
milestones.caption: 2090 · retirement. chose work part time over retire, because an earlier life learned: always set aside a small, consistent portion of income for future needs

milestones.reasoning: even though i'm tired and have debts, helping others brings me peace and purpose. it's what my brother gustavo always said mattered most.
milestones.thought: wrote down another family story today, felt good to share with beatriz over tea.
milestones.caption: 2100 · what to leave behind. chose volunteer while the body allows over rest, because an earlier life learned: turn grief into service for those who are hurting

milestones.question: you are eighty. the walking group meets every morning.
